newsitem.title: UK: MAID sees BT deal spur sales up to 20 times.
newsitem.headline: MAID sees BT deal spur sales up to 20 times.

text.p: M.A.I.D Plc, the UK electronic business information provider, said on Thursday it expected sales of its intranet solutions to jump by up to 20 times after announcing it was linking up with British Telecommunications Plc.

M.A.I.D, which said it had been in discussions with BT for the last 18 months, said it made sense for the company to provide content for intranet packages for corporate customers while BT took control of providing telecoms services support.
Analysts had estimated that M.A.I.D, which said it would pay BT a sales commission of no more than 30 percent, could sell around 30 intranet solutions this year and 60 next year before its BT deal.

But sales could soar if BT provides the necessary sales people and consultants to look at customers' networks and telecoms, order the telephone lines and sort out network servers, M.A.I.D's chief executive Dan Wagner said.

"I'd expect sales to be at least 10 times if not more -- probably twenty times (current estimates)," said Wagner. "I think BT has 66,000 business customers in the UK using Internet services today...You have to say this has a significant impact on our business."

In a brief statement ahead of an official news conference planned in September, M.A.I.D said the joint information services with BT would be launched on the telecom giant's new intranet service, Intranet Complete.

From September, BT intranet users will be able to access M.A.I.D business information products including Profound, Profound Intranet and Profound Livewire, which supplies news alerts to business professionals at their desks.

Additional services based on M.A.I.D's LiveWire service and InforSort technology indexing technology would also be developed to help companies manage and organise internal information, the group said.

M.A.I.D said it was releasing some information about the deal ahead of autumn because the market had heard it was planning a telecoms deal. International news and information company Reuters Holdings Plc said later it, too, would supply business information to BT.

Reuters said its Reuters Business Briefing database, which competes with some of M.A.I.D's services, would become the key information service on BT Intranet Complete, providing up-to-the-minute news and company data.
M.A.I.D's shares were trading seven pence stronger at 197.5p by 1400 GMT. Reuters' stock gained 2.5p to 603.5p.
